title: A present from Tama
setting: A Sunday afternoon, the first fine day after three days of rain. Yuki has dropped in on her elderly neighbour, Satou-san, and they're sitting by his open garden doors. His cat, Tama, has been sulking in the corner.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: satou-san, koko, honto ni igokochi ga ii desu ne.
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、ここ、ほんとに居心地がいいですね。
lines.kana: さとうさん、ここ、ほんとにいごこちがいいですね。

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. kyou wa yatto ame ga yande, kaze ga kimochi ii desu kara ne.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。今日はやっと雨がやんで、風が気持ちいいですからね。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます。きょうはやっとあめがやんで、かぜがきもちいいですからね。
lines.english: Thank you. Well, the rain's finally stopped today, and the breeze feels lovely.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: aa, honto ni kimochi ii. kyou wa watashi, kibun ga ii n desu.
lines.ja: ああ、ほんとに気持ちいい。今日は私、気分がいいんです。
lines.kana: ああ、ほんとにきもちいい。きょうはわたし、きぶんがいいんです。
lines.english: Ah, it really does feel nice. I'm in a good mood today.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: watashi mo, kyou wa kibun ga ii desu yo. demo, tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu.
lines.ja: 私も、今日は気分がいいですよ。でも、タマはずっと機嫌が悪いんです。
lines.kana: わたしも、きょうはきぶんがいいですよ。でも、たまはずっときげんがわるいんです。
lines.english: Me too, I'm in a good mood today. But Tama's been grumpy the whole time.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, tama-chan, kigen warui no? nande?
lines.ja: え、タマちゃん、機嫌悪いの？なんで？
lines.kana: え、たまちゃん、きげんわるいの？なんで？
lines.english: Oh, Tama-chan, are you in a bad mood? How come?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: mikka mo ame ga futte, zutto soto ni denakatta n desu yo. neko wa ame ga dame desu kara ne.
lines.ja: 三日も雨が降って、ずっと外に出なかったんですよ。猫は雨がだめですからね。
lines.kana: みっかもあめがふって、ずっとそとにでなかったんですよ。ねこはあめがだめですからね。
lines.english: It rained for three days, so she hasn't been outside at all. Cats can't stand the rain, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan, ame, mou yanda yo. soto, kimochi ii yo.
lines.ja: タマちゃん、雨、もうやんだよ。外、気持ちいいよ。
lines.kana: たまちゃん、あめ、もうやんだよ。そと、きもちいいよ。
lines.english: Tama-chan, the rain's stopped now. It's lovely outside.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: a, soto ni demashita ne. yatto desu yo.
lines.ja: あ、外に出ましたね。やっとですよ。
lines.kana: あ、そとにでましたね。やっとですよ。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: watashi wa, mou chotto koko ni ite ii desu ka? igokochi ga ii node.
lines.ja: 私は、もうちょっとここにいていいですか？居心地がいいので。
lines.kana: わたしは、もうちょっとここにいていいですか？いごこちがいいので。
lines.english: Mind if I stay here a little longer myself? It's so cosy.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: douzo douzo, zutto ite ii desu yo. a, tama, mou modorimashita ne.
lines.ja: どうぞどうぞ、ずっといていいですよ。あ、タマ、もう戻りましたね。
lines.kana: どうぞどうぞ、ずっといていいですよ。あ、たま、もうもどりましたね。
lines.english: Of course, stay as long as you like. Oh, Tama's back already.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan, nani motteru no? e, mushi? kimochi warui!
lines.ja: タマちゃん、何持ってるの？え、虫？気持ち悪い！
lines.kana: たまちゃん、なにもってるの？え、むし？きもちわるい！
lines.english: Tama-chan, what have you got there? Huh, a bug? Gross!

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tama kara no purezento desu yo. mou kigen ii n desu ne.
lines.ja: タマからのプレゼントですよ。もう機嫌いいんですね。
lines.kana: たまからのぷれぜんとですよ。もうきげんいいんですね。
lines.english: It's a present from Tama. She's in a good mood already, I see.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou, tama-chan. demo, kore wa kimochi warui yo.
lines.ja: ありがとう、タマちゃん。でも、これは気持ち悪いよ。
lines.kana: ありがとう、たまちゃん。でも、これはきもちわるいよ。
lines.english: Thank you, Tama-chan. But this is gross.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sumimasen ne. kimochi warui desu yo ne.
lines.ja: すみませんね。気持ち悪いですよね。
lines.kana: すみませんね。きもちわるいですよね。
lines.english: Sorry about that. It is gross, isn't it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: 今日は気分よかったのに。
lines.kana: きょうはきぶんよかったのに。
lines.english: And I was in such a good mood today.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: tama wa, kigen ii n desu kedo ne.
lines.ja: タマは、機嫌いいんですけどね。
lines.kana: たまは、きげんいいんですけどね。
lines.english: Tama's in a fine mood, though.

choices.english: Tama stays grumpy and won't go outside, even after the rain stops.
Tama goes outside, comes back with a bug for Yuki, and is in a good mood again.
Tama brings Satou-san a bug, and Yuki goes home feeling sick.

questions.explanation: Lines 4-6: Satou-san says Tama has been in a bad mood (kigen ga warui) because it rained for three days and she hasn't been out. Line 7: Yuki tells her the rain has stopped, and in line 8 she goes out. In lines 10-12 she's back with a bug, and Satou-san says it's a present from Tama and that she's in a good mood already (mou kigen ii). A is wrong: Tama goes out as soon as Yuki tells her the rain has stopped (line 8), and she cheers up. C is wrong: the bug is a present for Yuki (lines 11-12), and Yuki doesn't go home. In line 9 she asks to stay longer, and her kimochi warui means 'gross', not 'I feel sick'.

questions.english: It's a warm evening, and you and Kenta are sitting by the river when a breeze picks up. He asks, "kaze, daijoubu?" (Is the breeze okay?) Tell him you're fine: it feels nice.
questions.answer: Say you're fine and the breeze feels nice, with kimochi ii (ga usually drops in casual speech): un, daijoubu. kimochi ii yo.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm fine. It feels nice.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu. kaze ga kimochi ii ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫。風が気持ちいいね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine. The breeze feels lovely, doesn't it?

questions.explanation: kimochi ii is how something feels on your body: a breeze, a bath, a stretch. That's how it's used in lines 2, 3 and 7 (kaze ga kimochi ii, aa, honto ni kimochi ii, soto, kimochi ii yo). Don't say kibun ga ii here: that's your mood, as in lines 3-4. And a nice breeze isn't tanoshii (fun). Kenta is a friend, so answer casually; ne at the end asks him to agree, like the second model answer.

questions.english: Tama comes back carrying something, and Yuki cries, "e, mushi? kimochi warui!" What does she mean?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、なんで気持ち悪いと言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんできもちわるいといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande kimochi warui to iimashita ka?

choices.english: She thinks the bug Tama has brought is gross.
She suddenly feels unwell, as if she's coming down with a cold.
She thinks Tama is in a bad mood again.

questions.explanation: Line 11: Yuki says kimochi warui the moment she sees what Tama is carrying (e, mushi? a bug?), so here it means 'Gross!'. She says it again to Tama in line 13 (kore wa kimochi warui yo), and Satou-san agrees in line 14. B is wrong: kimochi warui can also mean queasy, but nothing has made Yuki ill, and for feeling unwell with a cold you'd say guai ga warui. C is wrong: a bad mood that shows is kigen ga warui, and by now Satou-san says the opposite, that Tama is already in a good mood (mou kigen ii, line 12).

questions.english: You've been smiling all afternoon, and Kenta says, "kyou, kigen ii ne. nande?" (You're in a good mood today. How come?) Tell him you're in a good mood, and why.
questions.ja: 今日、機嫌いいね。なんで？
questions.kana: きょう、きげんいいね。なんで？
questions.answer: Talk about your own mood with kibun ii (kibun ga ii), not kigen: un, kyou wa kibun ii n da. Then give a reason.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kyou wa kibun ii n da. ame mo yanda shi.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、今日は気分いいんだ。雨もやんだし。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm in a good mood today. The rain's stopped, for one thing.

modelAnswers.romaji: datte, shigoto owatta kara. kibun ii n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: だって、仕事終わったから。気分いいんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: Well, work's done! I'm in a good mood.

questions.explanation: Kenta sees your mood from the outside, so he says kigen ii, the way Satou-san talks about Tama in lines 12 and 16. About your own mood you say kibun ga ii, or kibun ii in casual speech, as Yuki and Satou-san do in lines 3-4 (kyou wa watashi, kibun ga ii n desu); Yuki uses the past in line 15 (kyou wa kibun yokatta noni). Don't say kimochi ii: that's a physical feeling, like the breeze in line 2. n da gives an explanation, which suits a reply to nande.

questions.english: Yuki and Satou-san both say they're in a good mood today. Then Satou-san tells Yuki how Tama has been. What did he say?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: さとうさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Tama's been feeling sick the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kibun ga warui n desu

choices.english: Tama's been queasy (or gross) the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kimochi ga warui n desu

choices.english: Tama's been in a bad mood the whole time.
choices.romaji: tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu

questions.explanation: Line 4: 'demo, tama wa zutto kigen ga warui n desu.' A bad mood that others can see, in a person, a child or a cat, is kigen ga warui, and Yuki echoes it to the cat in line 5 (kigen warui no?). In the same line Satou-san uses kibun only for his own mood (kyou wa kibun ga ii desu yo). A is wrong: kibun ga warui is what English speakers tend to say for 'in a bad mood', but it means feeling sick or put off. B is wrong: kimochi ga warui means queasy or gross. It's what Yuki says about the bug (lines 11 and 13), not what Satou-san says about Tama.

questions.english: You've been chatting at Satou-san's house all afternoon. He asks, "mou kaerimasu ka?" (Are you heading home now?) Tell him you'd like to stay a little longer because it's so cosy here.
questions.answer: Ask to stay a bit longer and give the reason with igokochi ga ii, politely: mou chotto ite ii desu ka? koko, igokochi ga ii node.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, mou chotto ite ii desu ka? koko, igokochi ga ii node.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、もうちょっといていいですか？ここ、居心地がいいので。
modelAnswers.english: No, could I stay a little longer? It's so cosy here.

modelAnswers.romaji: mada daijoubu desu. koko, honto ni igokochi ga ii n desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: まだ大丈夫です。ここ、ほんとに居心地がいいんですよ。
modelAnswers.english: I'm fine for a while yet. It's really cosy here.

questions.explanation: igokochi ga ii is for a place you feel at ease in, as Yuki says of Satou-san's house in lines 1 and 9 (igokochi ga ii node). Don't reach for kaiteki (comfortable), which is physical comfort and sounds like an advert, or kimochi ii, which is how the breeze feels on your skin. Satou-san is an elderly neighbour and speaks politely, so answer in desu/masu; node gives the reason softly.

newWords.english: Tama, Satou-san's cat (Yuki calls her tama-chan; -chan is a friendly name ending)
